conflicts.description: Lamp 62: the printed page 31 lamp drawing places 62 at the front/bottom bumper and 63 at the rear/right bumper. Both related VPX scripts bind 62 to the rear/right bulb body and 63 to the front/bottom body. The printed page 29 switch drawing separately places 50 rear/right and 51 front/bottom, matching the consumed sensor bindings despite their Bottom/Right labels. No independent socket wire trace or production lamp-test observation settles which lamp mapping is physical. Retain fitment and runtime bindings, and withhold the disputed physical coordinate. Resolution path: a production-machine owner or service technician can observe which bumper bulb lights for lamps 62 and 63 in the machine's lamp test, or trace each socket's lamp-matrix wire pair.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(63,64) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(63,64) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 64 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 64: a host write to 64 is overwritten on the next update. The local table and de.vbs drive public 82. Physical lower and upper SSFB boards are separate; the table moves both same-side flippers together.

inputs.label: PIA2 Port A Bit 7 Configuration Input

physical.notes: The shared driver exposes one DIP bank and pia2a_r supplies core_getDip(0)<<7 under a shared Jumper W7 comment. DE_COMPORTS declares no Country DIP. Bounded static analysis of all three CPUs verifies normal DDRA=$FF, which masks external PA7; reviewed IRQ reads discard it and the fatal blink loop masks output to bit4. Indexed/scheduler coverage gaps prevent a whole-program unused claim. Raw DIP0=1 probes are separate stimuli. No WWF physical jumper or country setting is established.

mechanisms.behavior: Six captive trough positions feed the right-hand release station (seventh contact). Coil 1 operates the separate 25-1240 lock-ball cam; coil 2 operates the 23-800 release plunger. Six subminiature contacts and one miniature release contact are physical, not optos. The table starts six balls in the stack, passing switches 14,13,12,11,10,9 to cvpmBallStack.InitSw after its zero entry-switch argument. Its coil-1 callback feeds a ball to BallRelease and coil 2 clears 15 and kicks toward the shooter. Keep the two actuators and the release contact separate. Ball movement, not a direct electrical coil-to-contact relation, changes the occupancy. A jam holds an occupied contact and prevents the expected transfer; table tuning is not a measured machine timing.
mechanisms.label: Six-ball trough and seventh release position

mechanisms.behavior: Ball occupies shooter lane 16; output 3 pulses the 50V auto-launch kicker. The retained script uses the Shooter saucer and a variable kick force. TAG is a separate cabinet switch 62 even though the virtual table maps its plunger key to TAG. Do not add an unsourced manual-plunger switch.
mechanisms.label: Shooter auto launch

mechanisms.behavior: The upper playfield's eject has a horizontal coil/plunger and a separate next-to-eject contact 28. Coil 4 kicks a ball from the table's sw28 saucer into the ring; 29 detects passage on the upper playfield. 29 is a ball-path sensor, not a coil position limit. No physical eject-home sensor is enumerated.
mechanisms.label: Upper ring eject

mechanisms.behavior: The right-side VUK captures a ball on 20; output 5 lifts it into the wire ramp. The local table uses sw20 for capture and sw20a for the kick. The coil chart calls this VUK and the switch chart calls 20 Super VUK; those names describe the same right-hand assembly. Spring return is mechanical; a pulse does not directly assert the ball contact.
mechanisms.label: Right VUK to wire ramp

mechanisms.behavior: Left/middle scoop balls pass the under-playfield trough contact 39 and arrive at the VUK's ball contact 40. Output 6 lifts the ball back to the playfield. The local script destroys the ball at sw39, pulses 39 for 200 ms, then adds a ball to the sw40 stack; that delay is a table approximation, not measured subway travel. The chart names coil 6 Super VUK but switch 40 Super VUK / VUK (Middle). Page 54 identifies the common left/middle assembly.
mechanisms.label: Left and middle scoop subway / super VUK

mechanisms.behavior: Four individually latched down targets ordered top to bottom D,A,E,D. Each target holds its own contact until output 7 lifts/reset all four. The table maps cvpmDropTarget in that order and closes a contact when its target drops. Start with targets raised; reset pulses restore them. A bank that does not rise leaves contacts closed and should remain detectable as a fault.
mechanisms.label: Lower left four-target D-A-E-D bank

mechanisms.behavior: Three individually latched drop targets ordered upper-playfield left, middle, right. Output 9 lifts the common reset bracket; contacts 30,31,32 follow the targets. The table's dtT InitDrop and SolDropUp preserve this order. The parts page's shaded two-target variants are not fitted to this game.
mechanisms.label: Upper ring three-target WWF bank

mechanisms.behavior: Rear-panel coil 32-1800 moves an armature/paddle against a 15 oz spring. No position switch is present in the complete assembly table or matrix. The local table's SolBackDiverter rotates its visual 0/40 degrees and a hidden collision flipper while enabled/disabled. Those angles and the hidden flipper pivot outside the playfield are table-owned; they are not physical coordinates or measured travel.
mechanisms.label: Rear panel ramp diverter

mechanisms.behavior: 27-1500 coil, spring, plunger, crank arm and left shaft/paddle 515-6023-00 route the upper-left ring entry. No position sensor is enumerated. The table drives Flipper3 plus LeftDiverter at 0/-35 degrees with output 13. Preserve the output level and ball routing; do not interpret the script's flipper helper as an extra physical flipper.
mechanisms.label: Upper playfield left diverter

mechanisms.behavior: 27-1500 coil, spring, plunger, crank and right paddle/shaft 515-6024-00. The exact script ignores disabled callbacks, starts RightDivT on enabled callbacks, alternates a divstate flag, animates 0 to 45 degrees and back on successive enabled commands, and swaps TRDiv1/TRDiv2 collision walls. Initial script flag is false and TRDiv2 is dropped at startup. This proves the retained virtual routing contract; it does not establish physical home orientation, whether the real paddle is held or toggled, or physical travel time. Keep mechanism_behavior missing until an operating production assembly can be observed against output 22.
mechanisms.label: Upper playfield right diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Two lower 22-1080 coils (500-5755-01 right / -02 left) and two upper 25-1800 coils (500-5820-01 right / -02 left). SSFB 1 serves lower and SSFB 2 upper, with 50V DC power and 8V AC hold supplies. The upper coil chart has no EOS; lower EOS is local hardware. PinMAME uses FLIP6364 without FLIP_SOL/EOS, copies host 84 to matrix 63 and 82 to 64 and fabricates 45/46 right and 47/48 left together while 23 is enabled. The ROM cannot consume the upper flipper-column bits. The exact table reads 46/48 and moves both same-side flippers together; independent physical staging and the power/hold waveforms are not represented by those synthetic pairs. No EOS simulation is needed by the emulated ROM.
mechanisms.label: Four flippers on two solid-state boards

mechanisms.behavior: Two three-standup T-A-G banks (amber left, yellow right) qualify Collect Tag; a separate captive ball strikes switch 47. The script creates a captive ball once and binds its trigger separately from the six standups. This captive ball is additional to the six free trough balls and is never inserted into the trough stack.
mechanisms.label: Captive ball and TAG target banks

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet shaker motor, PPB Q1/J8-11, no position sensor. Coil test names and drives output 16. The retained table comments out its shake callback, so that omission does not make the fitted motor unused. A recreation may provide the rumble effect from 16; strength and motor inertia are implementation-owned.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet shaker motor

mechanisms.behavior: Three 500-5227-00 turbo bumpers and two 500-5226-00 slings. Switches 49/50/51 name left/bottom/right turbo; 19/27 name left/right slings. WWF's Cycling Coils names public 17/18/19 left/bottom/right turbo and 20/21 left/right sling. These are ROM-controlled PIA special outputs; PinMAME's per-game ssSw array is empty, so a recreation animates its local rubber/bumper physics separately and does not assume the emulator synthesizes a coil from a host closure.
mechanisms.label: Three turbo bumpers and two slingshots

S11_PRINTERLINE exposes PIA2 port B here; no physical playfield load is fitted. Verified static printer code reads the $0A00 character buffer and writes PB after CRA IRQ2/CA2-ready. Stock s11 supplies no CA2 ready input, so the reviewed helper times out before its write. This explains bounded silent probes, not a whole-program unused claim or a reconstructed physical printer protocol.
